title: 2008 HMMT February Guts Problem 4
statement: Find the real solution(s) to the equation \((x+y)^{2}=(x+1)(y-1)\).

solutions.text: \((-1,1)\) Set \(p=x+1\) and \(q=y-1\), then we get \((p+q)^{2}=p q\), which simplifies to \(p^{2}+p q+q^{2}=0\). Then we have \(\left(p+\frac{q}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{3 q^{2}}{4}\), and so \(p=q=0\). Thus \((x, y)=(-1,1)\).
